tools.title: Accelerator
tools.summary: A drum machine that can only speed up, until it crashes and starts again.

tools.title: Intonarumori
tools.summary: Six hand-cranked noise machines, one for each family of noise, that you play by dragging their pitch up and down.

tools.title: Enharmonic
tools.summary: A quarter-tone melody machine in free metre, where every bar chooses its own length.

tools.title: Cut-up Hat
tools.summary: Your loop is cut into words, shaken in a hat and played back in the order the pieces come out.

tools.title: Automatic
tools.summary: Draw without stopping to think: your hand becomes a melody and an exquisite corpse in three parts.

tools.title: Neo-Plastic Grid
tools.summary: A grid of coloured rectangles you can hear: across is time, up is pitch, and each colour is an instrument.

tools.title: Building
tools.summary: Build a song floor by floor from Bauhaus shapes: blue circles, red squares, yellow triangles.

tools.title: Kinetic Rhythms
tools.summary: Three rotating rods sweep through points in space; every crossing is a note, so rhythm comes from motion, not mass.

tools.title: Zero of Form
tools.summary: Pure shapes float on white; each one is a held tone, and where they overlap your sample sparkles.

tools.title: Zaum
tools.summary: Type words that mean nothing in any language and a throat made of your sample sings them.

tools.title: Theory of Intervals
tools.summary: A film strip of short sound shots, where the biggest music happens in the cuts between them.

tools.title: BLAST / BLESS
tools.summary: Every instrument is a word on the wall: BLAST it and it hits hard and dirty, BLESS it and it turns soft and holy.

tools.title: Event Scores
tools.summary: A deck of Fluxus-style instruction cards; the machine performs whichever card is on top, then flips the next.

tools.title: Dérive
tools.summary: A walker drifts through a map of a city; each district has its own sound and the city’s pull picks the route.

tools.title: Painted Lines
tools.summary: Paint melodies by hand in screen-print layers; the loop prints one colour at a time, then all of them together.

tools.title: Vow of Chastity
tools.summary: One sample, no effects, no grid: you play it live by hand, and every rule you break goes in a public confession.

tools.title: Credo
tools.summary: Three coins tossed six times build an I Ching hexagram, and the hexagram picks the sound, its length and its loudness from a chart.

tools.title: Breath Squares
tools.summary: Four nested squares are four drones that breathe; colours that sit close together make their tones beat against each other.

tools.title: BECAUSE
tools.summary: A three-chord punk machine where your BECAUSE lines become the riffs and the shouted rhythm.

tools.title: Cyborg
tools.summary: Three boundary sliders (human/animal, organism/machine, physical/non-physical) blur one groove between flesh and code.

tools.title: Virus Matrix
tools.summary: A step grid that is also a living culture: a virus spreads through the pattern each cycle, corrupting the notes it touches.

tools.title: Change Nature
tools.summary: A chord machine where the rules of tuning are yours to edit: how many notes in the octave and how the overtones stretch.

tools.title: Auto-Destructive Loop
tools.summary: A loop that destroys itself as it plays; its slow death is the piece, shown as a wall of bananas turning from green to brown.

tools.title: Art Concret
tools.summary: Every voice is a written formula, step × a + b mod n, so the whole piece is constructed in the mind before a sound is made.

tools.title: Spatial Cuts
tools.summary: A painted drone is the canvas; slash it, and each cut opens a window through which your sample comes from the space behind.

tools.title: Matter Alive
tools.summary: Your sample is the ground: throw balls of mud, paint and paper onto its waveform, and every impact plays the sound at that spot.

tools.title: Bicho
tools.summary: A hinged metal creature: bend its plates and the angles between them become the intervals of its chord.

tools.title: Anthropophagy
tools.summary: Feed the mouth sounds from anywhere; it chews them into pieces and digests them into a new Brazilian rhythm.

tools.title: Ultra Metaphor
tools.summary: Fuse two sound images into one metaphor: the rhythm of one drives the body of the other, with every ornament stripped away.

tools.title: Strident Radio
tools.summary: Tune a wireless dial across a 1920s city: every station is a different broadcast of your sample, with static and howl in between.

tools.title: Zenith
tools.summary: An endless climb to the zenith: Shepard tones and a sample that rises forever but never arrives.

tools.title: Make It Bloom
tools.summary: Build a brand-new sound from nothing, one harmonic at a time, then let it flower through your own sample.

tools.title: Slow Cooker
tools.summary: Time-stretch your sample until it slows to near stillness, simmering it in grains that you season and leave to ripen.

tools.title: Repurpose Platform
tools.summary: Steer a vector between four futures and repurpose the machine itself: every corner is a whole groove, and you can always expand the map.

tools.title: Airport Loops
tools.summary: Seven loops of different, unrelated lengths drift in and out of phase, so the music never repeats in the same way.

tools.title: Idea Machine
tools.summary: Write wall-drawing instructions and the machine executes them blindly: each line drawn across the grid becomes a melody.

tools.title: No
tools.summary: A full, flashy groove that you take apart with thirteen NOs, until only an ordinary walking pulse is left.

tools.title: Maintenance
tools.summary: The music gets dirty and falls apart on its own; your job is to look after it, and the care itself becomes the rhythm.

tools.title: Mould
tools.summary: A rigid, straight step grid is slowly overgrown by mould, and wherever the mould spreads, the notes bend, drift and grow organic.

tools.title: Ornament & Crime
tools.summary: Decorate a plain melody with trills, turns and grace notes, but every ornament costs labour, and the bill and the fashion clock are always running.

tools.title: The Store
tools.summary: A corner shop of found sounds: every product on the shelves is a sound object, and whatever you put in your basket becomes the song.

tools.title: Scratch Orchestra
tools.summary: A crowd of amateur players, each with a little tune of their own, who come and go as you add them or send them home.

tools.title: Für Statik
tools.summary: A rickety machine of meshing gears; every tooth strikes a note, so the gear ratios turn into polyrhythms.

tools.title: Décollage
tools.summary: Three posters pasted on top of each other, each one a different groove; tear strips away to reveal the layers underneath.

tools.title: Poor Means
tools.summary: Four poor materials (wire, stone, water and rag) and only the energy of your hands: pluck, strike, drip and rub.

tools.title: Databend
tools.summary: Bend the raw data of your sample: shift its bytes, flip its bits, swap and repeat its blocks, and listen to the medium break open.

tools.title: Sound Masses
tools.summary: Gliding sirens drive great masses of sound; drag them through space and listen to them collide or push apart.

tools.title: Constellation
tools.summary: Place a few words on the page like stars: their positions make the rhythm and space, and their letters make the melody.

tools.title: Letter Drum
tools.summary: A drum machine made of letters: type a line and every character becomes a sung vowel or a percussive sound.

tools.title: Ecstatic Truth
tools.summary: One slider takes the same recording from plain fact to something slowed, stylised and staged.

tools.title: Both-And
tools.summary: A machine that refuses to choose: every musical decision is a pair of opposites, and in the middle you get both at once.

tools.title: Actual Life Journal
tools.summary: A diary you can dance to: a voice memo is chopped into emotional vocal hooks, laid over a field recording and house or two-step garage drums, and taken through intro, build, drop and break.

tools.title: Seed Garden
tools.summary: Plant sounds as tape loops of different lengths and let them drift in and out of phase, so the music is never the same twice.

tools.title: Gradual Process
tools.summary: Set a musical process going and listen to it run, as copies of one pattern drift apart, fill in or stretch out.

tools.title: Murmuration
tools.summary: Every bird in a murmuration is a sound: its height sets the pitch and its speed sets the level, and no bird leads.

tools.title: The Colour Keyboard
tools.summary: Paint a composition from points, lines, triangles, squares and circles, and a playhead plays it: the colour picks the instrument (yellow is a trumpet, blue a cello), the shape sets how each note is played, and white and black are two kinds of silence.

tools.title: Live Live
tools.summary: Play a whole live set from one pad sampler: chop a phrase across sixteen pads, record patterns and build to a drop.

tools.title: Endless Music Box
tools.summary: Tap and each note blooms, returns every cycle a little quieter, and carries on by itself when you stop.

tools.title: Closed Groove
tools.summary: Four virtual turntables: cut any sound into short sound objects, then loop, slow, reverse and trim them.

tools.title: Golden Angle
tools.summary: Every birth is a note, a rotating arm plays the seeds it passes, and a Fibonacci-word rhythm ticks underneath.

tools.title: Rayonist Rays
tools.summary: Objects send out coloured rays that bounce off the edges, and music happens only where the rays cross.

tools.title: Spoken Mantra
tools.summary: The speech is cut into words, you choose which words make the mantra, a piano listens to the pitch of each word and harmonises it, and the arrangement runs intro, mantra, build (the phrase shrinks to one stuttering word), a beat of silence, then a pumping house or two-step drop.

tools.title: Discreet System
tools.summary: Two short melodies of different lengths feed a long tape-delay loop, so every note returns quieter and darker for minutes.

tools.title: Row Matrix
tools.summary: One row of all twelve pitch classes is laid out as the full 12 × 12 matrix of its 48 forms (prime, inversion, retrograde, retrograde inversion, at every transposition).
tools.inspired: Composition with twelve tones related only with one another (1923)

tools.title: Tide Predictor
tools.summary: The tide at any harbour can be predicted as a sum of a few simple cycles set by the Moon and the Sun, each with its own period, size and timing.
tools.inspired: Nature: the tide as a sum of cycles (1872 to 1873)

tools.title: Plastic Unit
tools.summary: A grid sequencer of small shapes inside squares; mirror, invert and multiply the grid to make endless variations.
tools.inspired: The Yellow Manifesto: notes for a manifesto (1955)

tools.title: USB Folder
tools.summary: Cut a vocal into lines, reorder them, stack loops on house or garage drums and add each tune to an ever-growing folder.

tools.title: No Starting Point
tools.summary: The mixing desk is the instrument: level, pan, echo, tone and tape speed per track, a bus compressor where pushing one sound up pushes the others down, and a brush to paint parts of the tape out.

tools.title: Tonality Diamond
tools.summary: A diamond of pure tuning ratios you can walk through, pivoting between chords built up and chords built down.

tools.title: Dawn Syntax
tools.summary: Birds cut their sounds into syllables and sing them through grammars you can edit, as a dawn chorus builds.

tools.title: Merz Collage
tools.summary: Tear fragments out of six materials (a tram ticket, newspaper, wood, wire, a voice and a piano) and glue them onto a page that loops.

tools.title: Tube Brakes
tools.summary: Load any found noise (a brake, a kettle, a door hinge, a gull, a squeaky trolley) and a pitch tracker follows it.

tools.title: Long Now Bells
tools.summary: The bells are additive (church, harmonic or enharmonic partials) and a STRETCH control bends them into imaginary metals; your own sample can be the bell.

tools.title: Gradus
tools.summary: The old five-step method for learning counterpoint, as a machine that writes a fresh second line against a fixed tune.
tools.inspired: Gradus ad Parnassum: the five species of counterpoint (1725)

tools.title: Same River
tools.summary: A loop that stays the same while what it plays keeps changing, like a river whose water is never the same twice.
tools.inspired: Patterns in nature and philosophy (c. 500 BC)

tools.title: Pop Art Is
tools.summary: A pop-song factory driven by eleven giant word faders, from Transient to Big business.

tools.title: Emotional Frameworks
tools.summary: One vocal line in slot 1 runs through seven frameworks: lifted house, two-step, numb, panic in the club, gospel, a peak-time rave and a slow, meditative Secret Life space.

tools.title: Lantern Marsh
tools.summary: A map of a marsh you walk across, where distance decides what you hear and old sounds are composted into new ones.

tools.title: In C, Your Way
tools.summary: Each player works through the patterns in order and repeats each one as many times as they like, so the parts slide against each other, and a steady pulse of eighth notes on high C holds everything together.
tools.inspired: In C (1964), with its performing directions (1964)

tools.title: Zeno's Race
tools.summary: Swift Achilles can never catch the tortoise, because he must first reach the place the tortoise has just left.

tools.title: Make Way for Magic
tools.summary: Paint gestures on four layers without stopping to think, and the gestures play.

tools.title: Emotional Frameworks Live
tools.summary: One vocal line, seven emotional frameworks, and live VJ / digital signage visuals for the big screen.
tools.inspired: Standalone live edition of Manifesto Machines tool 77

tools.title: Fifty-Three Cells
tools.summary: Up to 12 players, 53 app-written cells, one pulse, and live visuals for the projector.
tools.inspired: Standalone live edition of Manifesto Machines tool 79

tools.title: Loose Parts Table
tools.summary: A tabletop of loose shapes you push around until a picture turns up. Add circles, arches, sticks and triangles, colour them from your own photo, shake the table and keep what works.
tools.whatYouDo: Tap a shape to drop it on the table, drag it about, turn and resize it, then export a PNG or SVG.
tools.inspired: Simon Nicholson's theory of loose parts (1971); Friedrich Fröbel's play gifts (1830s)

tools.title: Mirror Garden
tools.summary: Draw one line and watch it bloom into a pattern. Every stroke is copied round a centre point, from two-fold to twenty-four-fold, with or without mirrors. Paint with plain colours or with the colours of your own photo.
tools.whatYouDo: Draw with a mouse, finger or pen; change the number of folds and mirrors; let the wandering brush draw for you; export a PNG.
tools.inspired: The kaleidoscope, patented in 1817; Rangoli and kolam threshold drawings; Islamic geometric pattern

tools.title: Grid Kit
tools.summary: A poster maker built on a modular grid. Type your own words, set columns, rows, margins and a type scale, then drag blocks between grid cells until the layout clicks.
tools.whatYouDo: Write a headline, a line of detail and some body text, choose a grid and a scale, drag blocks to snap to cells, export a PNG.
tools.inspired: Mid-century modernist poster design; Classical page proportions

tools.title: Palette Lab
tools.summary: Build a colour palette from one colour you like or from a photo of your own, then check every pairing for readable contrast before you use it.
tools.whatYouDo: Pick a base colour or load a photo, choose a harmony, lock the swatches you love, shuffle the rest, and export CSS, JSON or a PNG strip.
tools.inspired: The colour wheel, first drawn in the early 1700s; Bauhaus colour courses (1920s); WCAG contrast guidance

tools.title: Turtle Playground
tools.summary: Steer a little turtle with a handful of words and it draws as it goes. Write your own commands, make them repeat, give them names, and watch shapes appear line by line.
tools.whatYouDo: Type commands like fd 100 and rt 90, press Run, then build up repeats and your own named procedures. Export the drawing as an SVG.
tools.inspired: The Logo programming language, first written in 1967; Floor-turtle robots used in schools in the 1970s and 80s

tools.title: Rule Garden
tools.summary: Plant a few cells, set two tiny rules about birth and survival, and watch a living pattern grow. Swap rules, paint new seeds, or grow a garden from your own photo.
tools.whatYouDo: Paint cells or seed them from a photo, pick or type a rule such as B3/S23, press Play, and export a PNG. There is a one-line mode for the 256 elementary rules too.
tools.inspired: The Game of Life, published in 1970; Early cellular automaton research from the 1940s

tools.title: Cut-Up Machine
tools.summary: Paste in your own words, cut them into pieces with digital scissors, and shuffle until a line you would never have written turns up. Lock the bits you like and shake the rest.
tools.whatYouDo: Paste a text (a diary entry, a shopping list, an email), choose how to cut it, shuffle, lock and drag fragments, then copy or save the new piece.
tools.inspired: Dada chance poems made by drawing words from a hat (1920); The cut-up method developed in Paris around 1959

tools.title: Tiny Adventure
tools.summary: Write a little text adventure and play it straight away. Make rooms, join them with exits, hide objects, set a goal, then type go north and see if your world holds together.
tools.whatYouDo: Edit rooms, exits and objects on the right, play your game on the left, and save the whole story as a file you can share.
tools.inspired: Early text adventure games of the mid-1970s; Classroom use of text adventures for reading and writing
